newsitem.title: UK: Most Euro oil swaps dip, mogas down $2 but fuel up.
newsitem.headline: Most Euro oil swaps dip, mogas down $2 but fuel up.

text.p: European oil swaps were mostly slightly easier on Thursday despite modest gains on Brent crude futures.
Brent CFDs held steady for next week, trading at 43 cents under June, but the following two weeks slipped a few cents to 42 and 34 cents under respectively.
Dealers said demand for crude remained good.
Gasoline swaps fell $2 a tonne to $195.50 for May and were $3.75 lower for June. Rotterdam barges traded at $197 for loading up to May 15 but otherwise the market was quiet.
July talked some $3.75 below June. Naphtha fell $1 a tonne to $177.50 for May.
Heavy fuel firmed $1 a tonne to trade around $83 for May barges. June was 50 cents higher but dealers said the thin physical market had dampened trade. Low sulphur was valued around $89 for May.

Jet premiums were flat with May bid at $24.50 a tonne above the IPE after trading at that level last Thursday. The third and fourth quarters were little changed at $27.50 and $31.50 above the screen respectively.
